hardware_answers.question: Has TIOCEXCL landed? While a helper holds a board, does a second open fail with EBUSY/'already in use', is esptool refused, and does this hold for both helpers? This is what the container-vs-host warnings depend on.

answers.answer: TIOCEXCL has landed in both helpers. While either holds a board: os.open gives errno 16 EBUSY, pyserial fails with '[Errno 16] ... Device or resource busy', and esptool read-mac fails with 'Could not open ..., the port is busy or doesn't exist.' (exit 2). The capture is not disturbed. A second C source for another radio gets '... is already in use by another capture (an esp32c5 source or another program holds it); a board captures with one radio at a time'. A remote helper for the same board and radio is not refused locally, though: Kismet closes the running source, and the new helper takes over (see problems). Cross-container, per pi-docker-test.log D3: 'host open of /dev/ttyACM0 as osh: ERR 16 Device or resource busy', 'PASS D3 host open refused with EBUSY while the container captures', and the container's 4 sources kept running.
answers.evidence: n2b.out, n5b.out, g1a.log (208 s), pi-docker-test.log lines 26-38.

answers.answer: TIOCEXCL has landed in the Python helper as well: while it holds a board, every other open gets EBUSY, esptool is refused, and a second helper on another radio is refused with 'already in use'. The exception: a second helper with the same definition makes Kismet close the running one (check 4). The cross-container direction is in pi-docker-test.log D3 (not re-run).
answers.evidence: p5.out; see check 4. The Python-as-holder direction was also seen in the C run's n2b.out.

hardware_answers.question: Can the Pi rows be marked as re-run with the final C helper, the Python helper on the Pi and the current firmware? This includes flashing a board as Flashing-the-Firmware says and then capturing.

answers.answer: Not re-run in this session. Old firmware with the Python helper was covered by the C run: ~/e2e/hw2 has o100.pybtle, o100.pyzigbee and f10ab*.py logs for 1.0.0 and 1.2.0. For the roll-up, the Python helper on the current firmware captured Wi-Fi on both bands, zigbee (TXTEST) and BTLE on the Pi; flashing was not repeated here.

hardware_answers.question: What are the Python remote helper's handshake timings (0.8 s settle, 2 s first open, 6 s no-answer reopen, 15 s give-up) and exact message texts, including the normal connected/opening/opened/capturing lines and the Troubleshooting table texts?

answers.answer: C local part only: a silent port gives 'silent: no answer, reconnecting' at about 6 s, and at 15 s the helper exits. Kismet shows only 'IPC connection closed'; the helper's text '<name>: no capture from the board on <dev> for 15 seconds; is it flashed with the esp32c5 sniffer firmware, and is nothing else holding the port?' is written to the IPC but never shown. Kismet re-opens 5 s later. The MODE->START gap in strace is 0.80-0.83 s.
answers.evidence: n15.log and strace, n1.log, strace 168599/168648 (MODE at 31.990 -> START 32.792).

answers.answer:
Python handshake on a silent board (ROM download mode via esptool --after no-reset chip-id), timed from 'opened':
- MODE WIFI at +0.10 s, START at +0.90 s, MODE again every 2.0 s.
- 'INFO: /dev/ttyACM2: no answer for 6 s, reopening' at +6.03 s. Later repeats are logged at DEBUG only.
- Reopen 1.0 s later.
- 'ERROR: esp32c5-ttyACM2: the board on /dev/ttyACM2 has not been capturing for 15 s (last: /dev/ttyACM2 opened)' at 15.26 s after connect.
- Reconnect 5.03 s later; the cycle is about 20.3 s.

The hopper sends CHANNELS every 200 ms even while the board is silent.

Kismet shows 'Kismet external interface shutting down: ...' and error 'remote connection triggered shutdown: the board on /dev/ttyACM2 has not been capturing for 15 s (last: /dev/ttyACM2 opened)'.

For comparison, a C local source logs 'esp32c5-ttyACM2: no answer, reconnecting' at +6.0 s and 'IPC connection closed' at +15.1 s. Kismet re-opens after 5 s, and once logged a doubled re-open counted as an extra failure.
answers.evidence:
Other Troubleshooting rows (p8.out, p8b.out, p5, p4):
- Normal start: 'connected, offering it to Kismet as <UUID>' / 'opening <port> for <radio>' / '<port> opened' / '<port> capturing'.
- Kismet SIGSTOP for 20 s: 'connection ended: no PING from Kismet for 15 s', 11.9 s after the STOP. After SIGCONT, Kismet dropped the first reconnect ('did not get a ping response from the capture', 'Error reconnecting ... - source closed'); the next one captured.
- close_source.cmd gives 'connection ended: Connection to remote host was lost.', NOT the table's 'Kismet shut the source down: <reason>'.
- Missing port: '/dev/ttyACM9 is not there; is the board plugged in? (waiting for it)'.
- Bad hop list: 'Removed 2 channels ...'.

The board was recovered with esptool chip-id (hard reset) and answered START with link type 127.

hardware_answers.question: Does a board on the sibling's 1.2.0 web-flasher image sync and capture Wi-Fi, zigbee and btle under both final helpers? What are the BTLE fix-up behaviour and message text, and the length checks (no false drops)?

answers.answer: Yes, on the Kismet side (the extcap part, id 130, was not run). Board D8:0C on the published 1.2.0 image synced and captured all three radios under the C local, C remote and Python remote helpers. Wi-Fi: 792 / 516 / 342 packets. Zigbee: 200/200 TXTEST frames each, link type 230. BTLE: 2536 / 1141 / 633 packets, with 13/12/12 devices. The board sends flags 0x0013 and a zero CRC. Every helper rewrites each record to 0x0C13 with a valid CRC (100% of 4,323 pcapng packets checked) and logs this once per helper connection, verbatim: '<name>: the board's firmware does not mark BTLE packets as CRC checked, so Kismet would drop them; the helper fills in the CRC and the flags (the board only reports packets whose CRC passed). Flashing current firmware makes this unnecessary'. In Kismet it reads 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a local source and 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a remote one. There were 0 'impossible length' drops and 0 error packets. The only differences from current firmware are the fix-up message and the 0x0013 flags on the wire.
answers.evidence: f10w.out, f10z.out, f10b.out, f10rb.out, f10zr.out, f10raw.json

A stock Kismet needs a stock build, which does not exist on the Pi. hardware_answers.question: Why did two boards that reported the 1.2.0 app version and compile time not answer START? Does the USB serial number (the MAC in the by-id name) stay the same whatever the firmware, and in ROM download mode?

answers.answer: Partly settled. The USB serial number (the MAC in the by-id name) stayed the same on current, 1.2.0, 1.1.0 and 1.0.0, through six esptool download-mode entries and RTS hard resets. The by-id symlink for D8:0C was never re-created: its mtime is still 'Sep 28 12:35' and it still points to ttyACM2. The published 1.2.0 image, freshly flashed at 0x0 on board A (38:44:BE:BF:D8:0C) with NVS erased, answered 'START <us> <nonce>' on the first attempt in every test (fwcheck, both helpers, raw 'START 0 abcd'). So the earlier non-answer by two boards reporting 1.2.0 is not a property of this image as published; its cause is not settled. The 20x START loop and the NVS backup diff were not run. Board B was not flashed.
answers.evidence: f10.flash120.out, f10.120.start.out, f10.120.raw.out, ls -la /dev/serial/by-id at each step

answers.answer: Partial: in ROM download mode the USB serial number, and so the by-id name, stays the same. It is the same with this project's firmware.
answers.evidence: After 'esptool --after no-reset chip-id' ('Staying in bootloader.', 'BASE MAC: 38:44:be:bf:d8:0c'), ls /dev/serial/by-id still showed usb-Espressif_USB_JTAG_serial_debug_unit_38:44:BE:BF:D8:0C-if00 -> ../../ttyACM2 (p8.out). The 1.2.0 and backup-image parts were not run.

hardware_answers.question: With the sibling's firmware 1.0.0 and 1.1.0, what happens in btle mode (and in zigbee mode on 1.0.0) with both helpers: the 'lost sync (the board sends link type X, not Y)' and 15 s message texts, and the retry cadence? Does Wi-Fi still work?

answers.answer: 1.1.0 (sha256 3453d366...): Wi-Fi 613 packets; Zigbee 200/200. BTLE fails: MODE BLE is silently ignored (no reboot, the stream stays link type 127). The C local helper then logs pairs once every 0.5-1.0 s (34 pairs in 40 s): 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 capturing (btle)' followed by 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256)'. At 15.5 s the helper exits and Kismet shows only 'Data source ... encountered an error: IPC connection closed' and 'Kismet will attempt to re-open the source in 5 seconds. (1 failures)'. It re-opens at +5.1 s, a cycle of about 20 s. The helper's own 15 s text never appears (see problems). The Python helper logs '/dev/ttyACM2 capturing' followed by '/dev/ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256)' every 0.9 s. At 15.6 s Kismet shows 'encountered an error: remote connection triggered shutdown: the board on /dev/ttyACM2 has not been capturing for 15 s (last: /dev/ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256))', and it reconnects 5.1 s later. 1.0.0 (sha256 6a9c108f...): zigbee and btle fail the same way ('... not 283' / '... not 256'). The Python zigbee give-up came at 23.1 s in the first cycle, not 15 s. Wi-Fi does NOT work: START is answered with link type 127, but 0 records ever arrive (0 packets in 40 s under Kismet, 0 bytes raw).

Not re-run in this session. Old firmware with the Python helper was covered by the C run: ~/e2e/hw2 has o100.pybtle, o100.pyzigbee and f10ab*.py logs for 1.0.0 and 1.2.0. A stock Kismet needs a stock build, which does not exist on the Pi. For the roll-up, the Python helper on the current firmware captured Wi-Fi on both bands, zigbee (TXTEST) and BTLE on the Pi; flashing was not repeated here.
answers.evidence: Coverage of the other checks in this session: p2-p21.

hardware_answers.question: Re-measure start and radio-switch times with the current helpers (with the 0.8 s MODE settle): a local source with the board already on the radio versus after a switch; Kismet start to first packets; one remote C helper hopping for 60 s (device counts).

answers.answer: Partial, C local. Launched->capturing is 1.05-1.50 s for the same radio and about 1.5 s for Wi-Fi<->802.15.4, BLE->Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi->BTLE, with 0.8 s of that the MODE settle. It is 2.5 s when the board USB re-enumerates, and in one case (n1) the BTLE switch failed entirely. Kismet start -> first Wi-Fi packet with two Wi-Fi boards: 2.20/2.20, 2.79/3.29 and 2.24/3.66 s. The Python helper took about 1 s from 'opened' to 'capturing'. The 60 s C-remote device count was not run.
answers.evidence: n1, n1b, n1c, g1a-c, g4 logs; rt-py-*.out.

answers.answer: Python helper radio switch, board 10:BD:A3:C8:7D:54 (the board whose Wi-Fi to BLE switch hung once under the C helper). All 25 switches succeeded. Opened to capturing, median: same radio 0.97 s, Wi-Fi to zigbee 1.23 s, zigbee to Wi-Fi 1.36 s, Wi-Fi to BTLE 1.23 s, BTLE to Wi-Fi 1.31 s. MODE to START gap: 0.80 s.
answers.evidence:
p12.out, min/median/max:
- wifi->wifi: start->capturing 1.07/1.23/1.52, opened->capturing 0.81/0.97/1.26.
- wifi->zigbee: 1.49/1.50/1.60, opened 1.23/1.23/1.34.
- zigbee->wifi: 1.62/1.62/1.68, opened 1.36/1.36/1.38.
- wifi->btle: 1.48/1.50/1.59, opened 1.21/1.23/1.34.
- btle->wifi: 1.54/1.57/1.61, opened 1.28/1.31/1.35.
No re-enumeration: 4 by-id links throughout.

The helper always sends MODE first, so even the same radio waits the 0.8 s settle. strace MODE->START: 0.803 s (p3) and 0.803 s (p8).

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: The C helper's 15 s give-up message never reaches Kismet: users see only 'IPC connection closed'
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: Seen in 4 of 4 local give-ups (o110.btle.log, o100.btle.log, o100.zigbee.log, earlier n15.log): 0 occurrences of 'no capture from the board', and REST error_reason is 'IPC connection closed'. The helper writes the text as v3 CMD_ERROR (strace in hw2/results/hw2/strace/esp32c5.283245 line 137). Kismet cfe427074's kis_external.cc:1037-1066 dispatch_rx_packet_v3 has no case for KIS_EXTERNAL_V3_CMD_ERROR.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: At capture_esp32c5.c:1383-1388, send the same text as a message before cf_send_error: cf_send_message(caph, errstr, MSGFLAG_ERROR). Kismet logs MESSAGE frames, and the per-source text then appears. Do the same for the cf_send_error at line 925. Until then, change Bluetooth-LE-Capture.md:86, Zigbee-and-Thread-Capture.md:123 and Flashing-the-Firmware.md:335 to say that a local source shows 'IPC connection closed' and is re-opened every ~20 s.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: The wiki says sibling 1.0.0 captures Wi-Fi, but on this hardware it delivers no Wi-Fi records at all
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: On D8:0C, 1.0.0 answered START with link type 127, then sent 0 records: 0 packets in 40 s with a C local hopping source (which still logged 'capturing (wifi)'), and 0 bytes raw after CHANNELS 6, CHANNEL 6, CHANNELS 1-13 and 1,6,11, before and after an esptool hard reset. On the same board, 1.1.0 gave 613 packets and 1.2.0 gave 792. Cause not isolated; the 1.0.0 source's capture path matches 1.1.0.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: Change the 1.0.0 row and sentences to: answers START but streamed no Wi-Fi frames on the test boards (ESP32-C5 rev v1.0); flash this project's image. Mark 1.1.0 as tested: Wi-Fi and Zigbee work, BTLE fails.

code_corrections.problem: ~17: 'a lock taken inside a container is not visible on the host'.
code_corrections.correct: With TIOCEXCL, esptool without sudo is refused (EBUSY) on a board a container captures from. esptool with sudo (CAP_SYS_ADMIN) is not refused, so stopping the container first is still required.
